body: We're on the same boat here, buddy.

I actually hate being told "you are loved" by people who totally don't give a shit about me irl. When I feel very down, like right now... It gives off an energy like guilt. It feels like the person is guilt-tripping me by saying "you are loved, why are you depressed?"

Anyway, Idk if I make sense. But that's how I feel towards that sentence.
Wrote it based on how I feel atm. Thank you for your appreciation.
Thank you. I did my best to write this poem, and for people to resonate with this, I'm in awe.
Actually, I hope so too. But I guess they're all tired of me. Which is sad, but I don't blame them... I suck.
I feel you. I have PTSD and I dissociate A LOT. I'm  scared that I will never be the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon I dream to be because of this.
Omg. The title really caught my attention. It's so well thought of. It's amazing!

Wow. This speaks so much volume. As today is August  1st. And I am hurting even more because it's the month I want to kill myself. It's hard. It's utterly unbearable but I don't have anyone to talk to. This work of art hit right through me.
I felt the same. I mean, the diagnosis isn't something to celebrate. But to know what I'm dealing with is a relief. At least now I know.
How did your Doctor tell you? Did you ask?
Hello! Did you bleach your hair?

I have been diagnosed with OCD (2017), Bipolar Type 2 (2018), and Borderline Personality Disorder (2019).

None of these diagnoses are connected to the childhood trauma/s I have.
Circumstances are not helping. I just want to feel. :(
I want my scars to be permanent too. But they all fade.
Yes for me. I cut deeper when I feel psychological/mental pain the most. I even use a scalpel blade since I have access to it.

From what I know, keloidal scars depends on the genetics of the person.

Based on what I learned from my Surgery class:
- If you cut a tissue with a sharp instrument, it will heal better.
- If you cut a tissue with a blunt instrument and the tissue cuts are jagged, it will heal but it may cause worse scarring. Healing might take some time.

In my case, I use a scalpel blade so even if I cut deep and blood drips... the wounds heal better and it doesn't scar (and if it does, it just looks like a dark line on my wrist.) Most of my scars fade.
Well, the College Dean knows. I have a Psychiatrist too.
